units.text: INT. RADIO STATION BOOTH - NIGHT
A small glass room above a shuttered strip mall.
Dials, cables, dead plants.
A red ON AIR sign glows above the window.
Beyond it, the darkened studio floor.
Out the far window, a truck stop's neon bleeds into the rain.
LEANDRO PACHECO, 40s, the overnight host, headphones around his neck, a thermos of coffee at his elbow, leans back in a creaking chair.
He moves the faders with the unthinking ease of fifteen years.
A pile of unopened mail beside him.
That was Patsy Cline, and you're listening to Night Drive on 94.7. Four-fifteen in the morning. Phone lines are open.
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: He flicks a switch.
A line blinks red.
First caller. You're on the air.
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: Hello, Leandro.
units.name: CALLER

units.text: Hello. What can I play for you tonight?
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: Nothing. I just wanted to hear you talk.
units.name: CALLER

units.text: Well. That's what I'm here for. What's your name?
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: You know my name.
units.name: CALLER

units.text: Leandro's smile fades by a degree.
He glances at the line indicator: caller ID reads NO SIGNAL.
I'm afraid I don't. Help me out.
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: It's been so long since you said it.
units.name: CALLER

units.text: He sits up.
Takes a slow sip of coffee.
Sets the mug down without a sound.
Let's go to a song, shall we? This one's for you, friend.
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: He thumbs the fader.
A soft ballad swells.
He mutes the mic, but the line is still open.
He doesn't hang up.
Are you still afraid of the water, Leandro?
units.name: CALLER

units.text: His hand freezes.
The headphones slide off his shoulder to the floor.
Who is this?
units.name: LEANDRO

units.text: Look behind you.
units.name: CALLER

units.text: He doesn't.
He stares at his reflection in the glass: the booth, the lamp, the empty studio beyond.
And behind his reflection, standing in the dark at the edge of the floor, a figure he cannot make out.
He reaches for the ON AIR switch.
Turns it off.
The red glow dies.
The line goes dead.
The song plays on to an empty room.
